vendors.name: Saab
vendors.blurb: Swedish defence and aerospace group whose Digital Air Traffic Solutions unit sells digital towers. Its system went into the first production remote tower, at Örnsköldsvik in 2015.

vendors.name: Frequentis
vendors.blurb: Austrian communications and tower systems supplier. Frequentis USA received FAA system design approval, with conditions, on 2 September 2026.

vendors.name: Kongsberg
vendors.blurb: Norwegian defence and technology group. Core developer of the remote tower system behind Avinor's NINOX programme and the NAV CANADA DAATS framework contract (through Kongsberg Geospatial).

vendors.name: Indra
vendors.blurb: Spanish defence and air traffic management supplier. Works with Kongsberg on Avinor's Bodø centre and supplies the Fintraffic multi-airport centre, HungaroControl's Budapest centre and AlUla.

vendors.name: Searidge Technologies
vendors.blurb: Ottawa-based digital tower and apron vision company, partly owned by NATS. Supplier at Vigo, Hong Kong, Manchester, Farnborough, Heathrow and the Changi prototype.

vendors.name: Adacel
vendors.blurb: Air traffic simulation and automation company. Took over the remote tower technology developed by Cybernetica for EANS in 2022.

vendors.name: FerroNATS
vendors.blurb: Spanish air navigation services joint venture of Ferrovial and NATS. Delivery partner with Searidge at Vigo.

ansps.name: Avinor
ansps.blurb: Norwegian airport operator and air navigation service provider. Runs the Bodø Remote Towers Centre.

ansps.name: LFV
ansps.blurb: Swedish air navigation service provider. Runs remote tower centres at Sundsvall and Stockholm.

ansps.name: NATS
ansps.blurb: UK air navigation service provider. Controls London City remotely from Swanwick and operates the Heathrow digital tower laboratory.

ansps.name: DFS and DFS Aviation Services
ansps.blurb: German air navigation service provider and its services subsidiary. Runs the Leipzig and Braunschweig remote tower centres.

ansps.name: HungaroControl
ansps.blurb: Hungarian air navigation service provider. Operates a remote tower for Budapest.

ansps.name: IAA (Irish Aviation Authority)
ansps.blurb: Irish air navigation service provider. Trialled multiple remote towers for Cork and Shannon from Dublin.

ansps.name: LVNL
ansps.blurb: Dutch air navigation service provider. Contracted Saab for remote towers at Groningen and Maastricht.

ansps.name: Naviair
ansps.blurb: Danish air navigation service provider. Chose an integrated remote tower and approach centre starting with Billund.

ansps.name: Fintraffic ANS
ansps.blurb: Finnish air navigation service provider. Announced a multi-airport remote tower centre at Vantaa in June 2026.

ansps.name: EANS
ansps.blurb: Estonian air navigation service provider. Has served Tartu from Tallinn since April 2023.

ansps.name: Oro Navigacija
ansps.blurb: Lithuanian air navigation service provider. Ordered a Saab digital tower for Vilnius in 2025.

ansps.name: PANSA
ansps.blurb: Polish Air Navigation Services Agency. Selected Saab's digital tower for Warsaw Modlin in July 2025.

ansps.name: Aena and ENAIRE
ansps.blurb: Spanish airport operator and air navigation provider. Vigo is Spain's first certified digital tower.

ansps.name: DSNA
ansps.blurb: French air navigation service provider. Selected Frequentis for a Toulouse centre and a first tower at Tours.

ansps.name: ENAV
ansps.blurb: Italian air navigation service provider. Inaugurated Italy's first remotely managed tower at Brindisi in 2022.

ansps.name: skyguide
ansps.blurb: Swiss air navigation service provider. Has reported plans for a remote tower at Geneva.

ansps.name: NAV CANADA
ansps.blurb: Canadian air navigation service provider. Running the DAATS programme with Kongsberg Geospatial.

ansps.name: DECEA
ansps.blurb: Brazilian airspace control department. Installed South America's first remote tower at Santa Cruz in 2019.

ansps.name: Airservices Australia
ansps.blurb: Australian air navigation service provider. Building the digital tower for Western Sydney International.

ansps.name: CAAS
ansps.blurb: Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore. Commissioned a smart digital tower prototype at Changi.

ansps.name: SANS
ansps.blurb: Saudi Air Navigation Services. Operates AlUla remotely from Jeddah.

ansps.name: FAA
ansps.blurb: US Federal Aviation Administration. Sets the design approval path for remote tower systems in the National Airspace System.

regulators.name: FAA
regulators.blurb: Publishes the remote tower systems concept of operations, operational safety assessment, allocation report, operational visual requirements and draft technical requirements, and evaluates designs at the William J. Hughes Technical Center.

regulators.name: EUROCAE
regulators.blurb: Publishes ED-240A, minimum aviation system performance standards for remote tower optical systems, which extends ED-240 with visual tracking and pan-tilt-zoom object following.

regulators.name: EASA
regulators.blurb: European Union Aviation Safety Agency. National authorities, such as Spain's for Vigo, certify individual systems.

regulators.name: ICAO
regulators.blurb: International Civil Aviation Organization. Global standards and recommended practices for air traffic services.

regulators.name: IFATCA
regulators.blurb: International Federation of Air Traffic Controllers' Associations. Professional body that publishes policy positions on remote towers.

regulators.name: CANSO
regulators.blurb: Civil Air Navigation Services Organisation. Industry body that publishes news and guidance from service providers.

programs.name: NINOX (Avinor Remote Towers)
programs.blurb: Avinor's programme with Kongsberg, signed 2015. 14 airports run from Bodø as of April 2025, seven more planned.

programs.name: LFV remote tower services
programs.blurb: LFV's centres at Sundsvall and Stockholm.

programs.name: Fintraffic multi-airport centre
programs.blurb: Seven airports from a Vantaa centre, announced June 2026.

programs.name: SESAR remote tower demonstrations
programs.blurb: EU research programme that co-funded multiple remote tower demonstrations.

programs.name: NAV CANADA DAATS
programs.blurb: Digital Aerodrome Air Traffic Services programme; Kingston first.

programs.name: FAA remote tower systems program
programs.blurb: System design approval path, testing at the Technical Center, and eligibility under the Contract Tower Program.

us_timeline: Leesburg Executive Airport tests a remote tower system (summer 2015).
Colorado announces Northern Colorado Regional as an FAA remote tower test site.
Air traffic services at Leesburg begin through the FAA remote tower program.
FAA publishes Remote Tower Systems Concept of Operations v1.0.
Operational Safety Assessment v2.7 published (Allocation Report v1.3 follows 16 Sep 2021).
Draft Advisory Circular v3.0 for non-federal remote tower systems.
FAA vendor information meeting on remote towers.
FAA discontinues the remote tower program at Leesburg.
Colorado DOT says the FAA terminated the Northern Colorado project in late 2023 after the vendor stopped work.

FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 signed. Reason summarizes Section 621: a defined design and operational approval process within 180 days, briefings through September 2028, and eligibility under the Contract Tower Program.
Remote Tower System Technical Requirements draft v5.0.
FAA page states remote tower systems are not currently approved for use in the NAS and lists no system design approval.
AIN: FAA tests systems at the Technical Center and selected RTX-Frequentis for design approval evaluation; no approvals issued yet.
Digital Tower Technology Coalition announces its priorities.
Military and Aerospace Electronics reports an FAA request for proposals for remote tower systems, a potential 50 units over five years, responses due 26 June 2026.
FAA grants system design approval to Frequentis USA, with conditions (as stated in AIP Program Guidance Letter 26-06).
FY27 Contract Tower Competitive Grant Program opens; digital towers are eligible if FAA-certified. Applications close 19 October 2026.
FAA Office of Airports issues PGL 26-06 on AIP funding of Digital Airport Traffic Control Tower systems. It does not grant operational approval.
Colorado Aeronautical Board hears that guidance was issued and design approval granted; award timing is described as uncertain.
